text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a common practice in modern software development. When developers write new code, they add it to a shared repository. A CI system then starts an automated build, which compiles the code and checks that everything works together. During this process, the system also runs tests automatically. These tests help catch issues early, before they become bigger problems. A CI pipeline usually includes several stages, such as building, testing, and preparing the software for release. By catching issues early, teams can fix mistakes quickly and deliver better software. This makes CI pipelines an essential part of many development teams today.
